title: Finite ideal products: coherence and twisted cohomology comparison
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal F$, with module direct image and pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], let $\mathcal H=f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $f^*\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ induced by $\mathcal J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ and $f^\sharp$, using the canonical structure-sheaf map $\epsilon_f:f^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ of [def-sfb-tensor-pullback-structure-sheaf-map] and the image construction of [def-trf-ideal-module-product-image]. Thus $\mathcal H$ is generated locally by products of sections pulled back from $\mathcal J$ with sections of $\mathcal F$. Likewise $\mathcal J\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G$ is the image of $\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$.
(1) $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal H$, and $\mathcal J\mathcal G$ are coherent, and $\mathcal J\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal H$ as submodules of $\mathcal G$.
(2) For $n\in\mathbf N$ put $\mathcal N_n=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, with $\mathcal N_0=\mathcal O_X$; likewise $(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_Y$. The modules $\mathcal N_n$, $f^*\mathcal N_n$, and $f^*\mathcal L$ are invertible; tensoring by either $\mathcal N_n$ or $f^*\mathcal N_n$ is exact. There is a canonical isomorphism $f^*\mathcal N_n\cong(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$, namely the recursive comparison of [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison]. The ordinary projection map
$$f_*\mathcal H\otimes\mathcal N_n\longrightarrow f_*(\mathcal H\otimes f^*\mathcal N_n)$$
is an isomorphism. On an open trivializing $\mathcal N_n$, its restrictions identify with the identity of $f_*\mathcal H$; it is the map multiplying a section of $\mathcal H$ by the pulled-back section of $\mathcal N_n$. The sheaf $\mathcal H\otimes(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$ is quasi-coherent.
(3) For every $p,n\ge0$, the equality in (1), the projection map in (2), and the edge map $e_{f,\mathcal M}:H^p(X,f_*\mathcal M)\to H^p(Y,\mathcal M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap](c) for $\mathcal M=\mathcal H\otimes(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$ give natural isomorphisms
$$H^p(X,\mathcal J\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})\cong H^p(X,f_*(\mathcal H\otimes(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}))\cong H^p(Y,\mathcal H\otimes(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}),$$
where cohomology is [pqf-def-cohomology]. No properness, surjectivity, or ampleness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $f$ is affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] to $f$ and $\mathcal F$ to obtain coherence of $\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal F$. Since $Y$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] implies that $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-ideal-product] to $(f,\mathcal F,\mathcal J)$: its image submodule is precisely the $\mathcal H$ in the statement, it is quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal J\mathcal G=f_*\mathcal H$ as submodules of $\mathcal G$. No injectivity of $f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_Y$ is used.

proof.text: The inclusion $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F$ has quasi-coherent source by Step 1 and coherent target by hypothesis. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], on the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$, therefore makes $\mathcal H$ coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] to this coherent module: $f_*\mathcal H$ is coherent on $X$. The equality of submodules from Step 1 gives coherence of $\mathcal J\mathcal G$. This finishes (1).

source.place: Tag 01Y1, lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient; Tag 01Y6, lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent; Tag 0B5V, coherence of the ideal multiple

proof.text: The structure module is locally free of rank one, hence invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. With the tensor-power convention of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] ($\mathcal N_1=\mathcal L$, $\mathcal N_{n+1}=\mathcal N_n\otimes\mathcal L$ for $n\ge1$, and likewise for $f^*\mathcal L$), induction on $n\ge1$, using the tensor-product and pullback clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], shows that $\mathcal N_n$, $f^*\mathcal N_n$ and $f^*\mathcal L$ are invertible; for $n=0$, $\mathcal N_0=\mathcal O_X$ is invertible and $f^*\mathcal N_0\cong\mathcal O_Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. The canonical comparison $c_n:f^*\mathcal N_n\xrightarrow\sim(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$ is constructed recursively: $c_0=\epsilon_f:f^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ is the structure-sheaf pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], $c_1$ is the identity of $f^*\mathcal L$, and for $n\ge1$, $c_{n+1}$ is $f^*(\mathcal N_n\otimes\mathcal L)\cong f^*\mathcal N_n\otimes f^*\mathcal L\xrightarrow{c_n\otimes1}(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}\otimes f^*\mathcal L$. These comparisons are natural and send pulled-back pure tensors to the corresponding tensors of pulled-back sections by the section formula of the cited tensor comparison.

proof.text: Tensoring by either of the invertible modules $\mathcal N_n$ on $X$ and $f^*\mathcal N_n$ on $Y$ is exact: on an open where the module is identified with the structure module, the tensor functor is naturally the identity. Thus a short exact sequence stays exact on a trivializing open cover, and is exact as a sequence of sheaves since exactness can be checked locally (kernels and local images agree there). This proves the exactness assertions of (2), including $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B5V, exactness of tensoring with an invertible module; direct local verification

proof.text: Put $N=\mathcal N_n$. Construct the projection map from the compatible bilinear maps on opens $U\subseteq X$ sending $h\otimes s$ to $h\otimes f^*s$ on $f^{-1}U$; the universal property of the sheafified tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] makes this a sheaf map $P:f_*\mathcal H\otimes N\to f_*(\mathcal H\otimes f^*N)$. Choose a local generator $e$ of $N$ on $U$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. Pulling back the isomorphism $\mathcal O_U\to N|_U$, $a\mapsto ae$, along $f^{-1}U\to U$ (pullback is compatible with restriction to opens, [def-pc-module-pullback]) and composing with the structure-sheaf isomorphism $\epsilon:f^*\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_{f^{-1}U}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] shows that the pullback generator $f^*e$ trivializes $f^*N$ on $f^{-1}U$. Under $h\mapsto h\otimes e$ on the source and $h\mapsto h\otimes f^*e$ on the target, $P|_U$ is the identity of $(f_*\mathcal H)|_U$. Its local inverses glue: replacing $e$ by $ae$ for a unit $a$ multiplies both tensor coordinates by $a$, since $h\otimes f^*(ae)=f^*a\,h\otimes f^*e$. Thus $P$ is the asserted isomorphism. The formula also shows its naturality in $\mathcal H$ and in maps of the invertible factor, without any hypothesis on $f$.

source.place: Tag 01E8, lemma-projection-formula, degree-zero local argument; its omitted gluing is written here for rank one

proof.text: The module $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent by Step 1. The module $f^*\mathcal L$ is invertible by Step 3, hence quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]; its nonnegative tensor powers are invertible by Step 3 and therefore quasi-coherent as well. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] on $Y$ to $\mathcal H$ and $(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$. It gives quasi-coherence of $\mathcal M_n=\mathcal H\otimes(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n}$, completing (2).

source.place: Tag 01I8, lemma-widetilde-constructions (1); Section 01LA, tensor products of quasi-coherent modules

proof.text: Compose the equality of Step 1, the projection isomorphism $P$ of Step 5, and $f_*(1_{\mathcal H}\otimes c_n)$ of Step 3 to obtain $\alpha_n:\mathcal J\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal N_n\xrightarrow\sim f_*\mathcal M_n$. Apply the functor $H^p(X,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] to get the first isomorphism in (3). Since $f$ is affine and $\mathcal M_n$ is quasi-coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] applies and says exactly that the specified edge map $e_{f,\mathcal M_n}$ is an isomorphism, giving the second one. For a map $v_0:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, multiplication gives $v_0(af)=a\,v_0(f)$, so it restricts to $h:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H'$ and $f_*v_0$ restricts to $w:\mathcal J\mathcal G\to\mathcal J\mathcal G'$. Put $v=h\otimes1:\mathcal M_n\to\mathcal M'_n$. The local formula of Step 5 gives $f_*v\circ\alpha_n=\alpha'_n\circ(w\otimes1_{\mathcal N_n})$. Functoriality of cohomology and the coefficient-composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] give $H^p(Y,v)e_{f,\mathcal M_n}=e_{f,\mathcal M'_n}H^p(X,f_*v)$. Thus the displayed composite is natural. The same local tensor formula handles maps of invertible factors. The proof used only finiteness of $f$, local Noetherianity, coherence, quasi-coherence of the ideal, and invertibility.
